name: Premier Properties of New Brunswick
what_they_do: Landlord/manager of its own new-construction apartment buildings in New Brunswick aimed at Rutgers students, with an availability-and-pricing list by building, a resident portal for rent and maintenance, and press coverage of city growth.
customers: Rutgers students and their parents renting studio through three-bedroom apartments in New Brunswick; secondarily local residents looking for downtown housing.

size_signals.signal: Multiple buildings listed with per-unit pricing (191 Hamilton St, 17 Mine St, 15/32/40/50 Union St, and more)
General manager inbox published (generalmanager@premiernb.com) plus a resident portal
Around 100+ Google reviews reported by review aggregators

listing.platform: Google (as reported by Birdeye/apartments.com; not read directly from Maps)

website_review.primary_cta: 'PAY RENT' button (existing tenants) and 'VIEW AVAILABILITIES'; nothing on the home page pushes a prospective renter to enquire
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: No online application or tour booking - the pricing page says 'CALL FOR DETAILS'; contact form (first name, last name, email, message) with no phone field
website_review.trust_signals: Real building photography, published per-unit pricing with availability dates, press mentions (NJBIZ, Movoto), resident portal, awards page
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Footer says '© 2022 All Rights Reserved'; home page hero is a full-bleed photo with no headline or text above the fold
website_review.search_basics: Home title is 'Home - Premier Properties of New Brunswick' with a decent meta description; buildings have their own pages, but the 'AVAILABILITY AND PRICING' URL /availability-and-pricing 404s while the working one is /pricing-list
top_issues: Mobile layout is not responsive: at 390px the page renders 768px wide (scrollWidth 768, body 768), so content and nav are clipped off-screen
No headline or sentence of text above the fold - a visitor or agent cannot tell what the company does without scrolling
A guessed primary nav URL 404s, and the primary flow is 'PAY RENT' for existing tenants rather than a booking path for prospects
Copyright 2022 and no review widget despite 100+ reviews

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt allows everything and even sets Content-Signal ai-input=yes, sitemap exists. Hours (M-F 9-5), NAP and unit-level prices with availability dates are real text, which is genuinely good. But JSON-LD is a bare WebSite node with no LocalBusiness/address/hours, the site is not mobile-responsive, and there is no online application or tour booking - only 'CALL FOR DETAILS' and an email form with no phone field.

operations_signals.signal: Every prospect must call for availability, so leasing staff repeat the same price/availability answers per enquiry
Contact form captures no phone number, guaranteeing an email round-trip before anyone can call back
Rent payment and maintenance requests already run through a self-serve resident portal

top_opportunities.opportunity: Make the site responsive and add a real headline plus a per-building 'check availability / book a tour' flow - the biggest revenue leak for a student-rental business
top_opportunities.evidence: scrollWidth 768 at a 390px viewport; pricing page says 'CALL FOR DETAILS'; no application or tour booking

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add LocalBusiness/ApartmentComplex JSON-LD with hours, address and per-building prices so AI agents can answer 'what does a 2-bed cost and when is it free'
top_opportunities.evidence: JSON-LD is WebSite-only although prices and hours exist as plain text

top_opportunities.opportunity: Automate enquiry follow-up and add a phone field plus an instant availability reply, so after-hours student enquiries get answered
top_opportunities.evidence: Contact form lacks a phone field; office hours M-F 9-5 only; 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester'

scores.reasons: Gap: broken mobile layout, no above-fold offer, a 404 link, no booking - but good pricing data to build on. Ability to pay: manages multiple downtown buildings at $1,500-$4,200/month, so one extra lease pays for the work. Ease: a responsive rebuild of a small site plus booking setup is well scoped. Evidence: rendered every page at desktop and 390px, measured scrollWidth, tested nav URLs.
